title: Can you look big with a small frame? (theoretical aspects)
summary: Standing demonstration of what a small frame means, using his own short clavicles and narrow shoulders and back. Small frames look thicker but lack natural width; rather than chase the wide look, prioritise the muscles around the outline (triceps long head, medial/rear delts, traps) and limb development to create the illusion of width.

claims.claim: Muscles attach to the skeleton via tendons, so skeleton size and width heavily influence how you look and how a natural should train for a massive physique.
He is about 6 feet and around 210 lbs and looks fairly big, but objectively has a very short frame with narrow shoulders.
Short clavicles mean narrow shoulders, since pecs and delts attach to the clavicle; that means less natural width, a less impressive V-taper, and a narrower back.
A small frame can be advantageous because muscle on a small attachment area looks thicker as it grows.

Small-framed lifters shouldn't chase the look of wide-shouldered guys; they should grow the muscles around the outline: triceps long head, the three delt heads (especially medial and rear), and the traps.
You have to play the hand you're dealt; denying a small frame leads nowhere.
Small-framed people should focus on limb development: big arms extending to the side mask a lack of natural width.
Wide-framed lifters may lack thickness and look thin from the side, a separate problem he plans to address.
No matter what frame you are gifted with, you can look big.
